html:
On 19 August 1953 the elected prime minister of Iran, Mohammad Mosaddegh, was overthrown in a coup organised by the American CIA and British intelligence, with Iranian army officers and paid crowds.

In 1951 Mosaddegh had nationalised Iran's oil, run until then by the British Anglo-Iranian Oil Company. Britain answered with a blockade of Iranian oil, and the United States came to fear Iran would fall to the communists. A first attempt failed and the shah fled to Rome; days later the second succeeded.

Mohammad Reza Shah came back and ruled with growing power for 25 years. Mosaddegh spent his life under house arrest. Memory of the coup fed the anger behind the Iranian Revolution of 1979. The CIA admitted its role in 2013.
sum: On 19 August 1953 the elected prime minister of Iran, Mohammad Mosaddegh, was overthrown in a coup organised by the American CIA and British intelligence, with Iranian army officers and paid crowds.
